sanskrit: anāryatvam anācāraḥ krūratvaṃ niṣkriyātmatā puruṣaṃ vyañjayantīha loke kaluṣayonijam
english: Ignobility, lack of right conduct, cruelty, and a nature averse to duty—these reveal, here in the world, the man born of a tainted womb.

sanskrit: pitryaṃ vā bhajate śīlaṃ mātṛjaṃ vā tathobhayam na kathaṃ cana saṃkīrṇaḥ prakṛtiṃ svāṃ niyacchati
english: He takes up either the disposition derived from his father, or that from his mother, or both alike; but one of mixed origin can in no way hold his own true nature in check.

sanskrit: yathaiva sadṛśo rūpe mātāpitror hi jāyate vyāghraś citrais tathā yoniṃ puruṣaḥ svāṃ niyacchati
english: Just as a tiger is born resembling its mother and father in form, with its markings, so too a man conforms to his own womb of origin.

sanskrit: kulasrotasi saṃchanne yasya syād yonisaṃkaraḥ saṃśrayaty eva tacchīlaṃ naro 'lpam api vā bahu
english: Though the lineage's stream be concealed, the man whose origin is of mixed birth still cleaves to that disposition, whether in small measure or great.

sanskrit: āryarūpasamācāraṃ carantaṃ kṛtake pathi svavarṇam anyavarṇaṃ vā svaśīlaṃ śāsti niścaye
english: Even of one who walks a counterfeit path, bearing the appearance and conduct of the noble, his own innate character determines for certain whether he belongs to his own class or another.

sanskrit: nānāvṛtteṣu bhūteṣu nānākarmarateṣu ca janmavṛttasamaṃ loke suśliṣṭaṃ na virajyate
english: Among beings of varied conduct, devoted to varied works, that which is well-joined in the world—where birth and conduct match—does not fall away.

sanskrit: śarīram iha sattvena narasya parikṛṣyate jyeṣṭhamadhyāvaraṃ sattvaṃ tulyasattvaṃ pramodate
english: Here a man's body is drawn along by its inner nature—be that nature highest, middling, or lowest; and like delights in like nature.

sanskrit: jyāyāṃsam api śīlena vihīnaṃ naiva pūjayet api śūdraṃ tu sadvṛttaṃ dharmajñam abhipūjayet
english: One should not honor even a person of higher standing who is wanting in good character; but a Śūdra of virtuous conduct, knowing dharma, one should indeed honor.

sanskrit: ātmānam ākhyāti hi karmabhir naraḥ; svaśīlacāritrakṛtaiḥ śubhāśubhaiḥ pranaṣṭam apy ātmakulaṃ tathā naraḥ; punaḥ prakāśaṃ kurute svakarmabhiḥ
english: A man proclaims himself by his deeds, good and ill, wrought by his own disposition and conduct; and so a man, though his own lineage be lost to sight, brings it again to light by his own actions.

sanskrit: yoniṣv etāsu sarvāsu saṃkīrṇāsv itarāsu ca yatrātmānaṃ na janayed budhas tāḥ parivarjayet
english: Among all these wombs of origin, both the mixed and the others, the wise man should shun those in which he ought not to beget himself.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brūhi putrān kuruśreṣṭha varṇānāṃ tvaṃ pṛthak pṛthak kīdṛśyāṃ kīdṛśāś cāpi putrāḥ kasya ca ke ca te
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me, O best of the Kurus, of the sons of the several classes, each apart—from what kind of woman, and of what kind, are the sons of whom, and who are they?

sanskrit: vipravādāḥ subahuśaḥ śrūyante putrakāritāḥ atra no muhyatāṃ rājan saṃśayaṃ chettum arhasi
english: Many conflicting opinions are heard concerning the matter of sons; here, O king, you must cut away the doubt of those who are bewildered.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ātmā putras tu vijñeyas tasyānantarajaś ca yaḥ niyuktajaś ca vijñeyaḥ sutaḥ prasṛtajas tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: The son born of oneself is to be known, and he who is born next after him; and the son begotten under appointment is to be known, and likewise the son born of one cast off.

sanskrit: patitasya ca bhāryāyāṃ bhartrā susamavetayā tathā dattakṛtau putrāv adhyūḍhaś ca tathāparaḥ
english: And the son born to the wife of a fallen man, lawfully united by a husband; and the two sons, the given and the made; and yet another, the son brought with a married bride.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ apadhvaṃsajāś cāpi kānīnāpasadās tathā ity ete te samākhyātās tān vijānīhi bhārata
english: And the six born of degradation, and the son of an unwed maiden, and the lowborn—these have thus been declared to you; know them, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ṣaḍ apadhvaṃsajāḥ ke syuḥ ke vāpy apasadās tathā etat sarvaṃ yathātattvaṃ vyākhyātuṃ me tvam arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who are the six born of degradation, and who again are the lowborn? All this, in accordance with the truth, you must expound to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca triṣu varṇeṣu ye putrā brāhmaṇasya yudhiṣṭhira varṇayoś ca dvayoḥ syātāṃ yau rājanyasya bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: The sons whom a Brāhmaṇa begets upon the three other classes, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and the two whom a Kṣatriya begets upon the two classes, O Bhārata—

sanskrit: eko dvivarṇa evātha tathātraivopalakṣitaḥ ṣaḍ apadhvaṃsajās te hi tathaivāpasadāñ śṛṇu
english: and the one whom the man of two classes begets—thus reckoned here, these are the six born of degradation. Now hear likewise of the lowborn.

sanskrit: caṇḍālo vrātyavenau ca brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāsu ca vaiśyāyāṃ caiva śūdrasya lakṣyante 'pasadās trayaḥ
english: The Caṇḍāla, and the Vrātya and the Vena—the three lowborn of a Śūdra are marked out, born respectively upon a Brāhmaṇa woman, upon a Kṣatriya woman, and upon a Vaiśya woman.

sanskrit: māgadho vāmakaś caiva dvau vaiśyasyopalakṣitau brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāyāṃ ca kṣatriyasyaika eva tu
english: The Māgadha and the Vāmaka, the two reckoned as a Vaiśya's, born upon a Brāhmaṇa woman and a Kṣatriya woman; and the Kṣatriya's is but one—

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyāṃ lakṣyate sūta ity ete 'pasadāḥ smṛtāḥ putrareto na śakyaṃ hi mithyā kartuṃ narādhipa
english: the Sūta, marked out as born upon a Brāhmaṇa woman. These are remembered as the lowborn; for the seed that makes a son cannot be made false, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kṣetrajaṃ ke cid evāhuḥ sutaṃ ke cit tu śukrajam tulyāv etau sutau kasya tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Some declare the son to be the field-born, others the seed-born; of which of the two are these equally sons? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca retajo vā bhavet putras tyakto vā kṣetrajo bhavet adhyūḍhaḥ samayaṃ bhittvety etad eva nibodha me
english: Bhīṣma said: A son may be born of the seed, or, being abandoned, may be field-born; or he may be the adhyūḍha, born when a compact is broken—learn this from me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca retojaṃ vidma vai putraṃ kṣetrajasyāgamaḥ katham adhyūḍhaṃ vidma vai putraṃ hitvā ca samayaṃ katham
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The son born of the seed we know; but how comes the field-born to be? And how do we know the adhyūḍha son, born when a compact has been set aside?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ātmajaṃ putram utpādya yas tyajet kāraṇāntare na tatra kāraṇaṃ retaḥ sa kṣetrasvāmino bhavet
english: Bhīṣma said: When a man, having begotten his own son, abandons him for some other cause, the seed is no longer the deciding factor there; that son belongs to the lord of the field.

sanskrit: putrakāmo hi putrārthe yāṃ vṛṇīte viśāṃ pate tatra kṣetraṃ pramāṇaṃ syān na vai tatrātmajaḥ sutaḥ
english: For when a man desiring a son, for a son's sake, takes a woman, O lord of peoples, there the field is the measure, and the son is not reckoned as begotten of his own seed.

sanskrit: anyatra kṣetrajaḥ putro lakṣyate bharatarṣabha na hy ātmā śakyate hantuṃ dṛṣṭāntopagato hy asau
english: In another case the son is marked as field-born, O bull of the Bharatas; for one's own self cannot be slain—this is borne out by the established example.

sanskrit: kaś cic ca kṛtakaḥ putraḥ saṃgrahād eva lakṣyate na tatra retaḥ kṣetraṃ vā pramāṇaṃ syād yudhiṣṭhira
english: And some son is the made one, recognized merely by adoption; there neither seed nor field is the measure, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kīdṛśaḥ kṛtakaḥ putraḥ saṃgrahād eva lakṣyate śukraṃ kṣetraṃ pramāṇaṃ vā yatra lakṣyeta bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what kind is the made son, recognized merely by adoption, where neither seed nor field is found to be the measure, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mātāpitṛbhyāṃ saṃtyaktaṃ pathi yaṃ tu pralakṣayet na cāsya mātāpitarau jñāyete sa hi kṛtrimaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: One whom a man finds abandoned by mother and father upon the road, and whose mother and father are not known—he is the made son.

sanskrit: asvāmikasya svāmitvaṃ yasmin saṃpratilakṣayet savarṇas taṃ ca poṣeta savarṇas tasya jāyate
english: In whom one establishes ownership over the ownerless, and a man of the same class rears him, that son becomes of the same class as his rearer.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca katham asya prayoktavyaḥ saṃskāraḥ kasya vā katham deyā kanyā kathaṃ ceti tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How is the sacrament to be performed for him, and after whose manner, and how? And how is a maiden to be given to him? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ātmavat tasya kurvīta saṃskāraṃ svāmivat tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: One should perform the sacrament for him as for one's own son, and so according to the rearer's standing.

sanskrit: tyakto mātāpitṛbhyāṃ yaḥ savarṇaṃ pratipadyate tad gotravarṇatas tasya kuryāt saṃskāram acyuta
english: He who, abandoned by mother and father, comes to a man of the same class—for him one should perform the sacrament according to that man's lineage and class, O unfaltering one.

sanskrit: atha deyā tu kanyā syāt tadvarṇena yudhiṣṭhira saṃskartuṃ mātṛgotraṃ ca mātṛvarṇaviniścaye
english: Then the maiden is to be given according to that man's class, O Yudhiṣṭhira; and where the mother's class is determined, the rites are to be done by the mother's lineage.

sanskrit: kānīnādhyūḍhajau cāpi vijñeyau putrakilbiṣau tāv api svāv iva sutau saṃskāryāv iti niścayaḥ
english: The son of an unwed maiden and the son brought with a married bride are likewise to be known as flawed sons; yet the settled rule is that these two also are to be consecrated as though they were one's own sons.

sanskrit: kṣetrajo vāpy apasado ye 'dhyūḍhās teṣu cāpy atha ātmavad vai prayuñjīran saṃskāraṃ brāhmaṇādayaḥ
english: And whether field-born or lowborn, those who are the adhyūḍhas—for these too the Brāhmaṇas and the rest should perform the sacrament as for their own sons.

sanskrit: dharmaśāstreṣu varṇānāṃ niścayo 'yaṃ pradṛśyate etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: This is the settled rule concerning the classes as shown in the books of dharma. All this has been declared to you; what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca darśane kīdṛśaḥ snehaḥ saṃvāse ca pitāmaha mahābhāgyaṃ gavāṃ caiva tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What sort of affection arises in the seeing of cattle and in dwelling with them, O grandsire, and what is the great blessedness of cows? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi purāvṛttaṃ mahādyute nahuṣasya ca saṃvādaṃ maharṣeś cyavanasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Come then, I shall relate to you an event of olden days, O greatly radiant one—the colloquy between Nahuṣa and the great sage Cyavana.

sanskrit: purā maharṣiś cyavano bhārgavo bharatarṣabha udavāsakṛtārambho babhūva sumahāvrataḥ
english: Of old, O bull of the Bharatas, the great sage Cyavana of Bhṛgu's line, having undertaken a dwelling in the waters, became one of mighty vow.

sanskrit: nihatya mānaṃ krodhaṃ ca praharṣaṃ śokam eva ca varṣāṇi dvādaśa munir jalavāse dhṛtavrataḥ
english: Having slain pride and anger, and elation and grief as well, the sage held fast to his vow of dwelling in the water for twelve years.

sanskrit: ādadhat sarvabhūteṣu visrambhaṃ paramaṃ śubham jalecareṣu sattveṣu śītaraśmir iva prabhuḥ
english: He bestowed upon all beings the highest, most blessed trust, even upon the creatures that move in the water, like the cool-rayed lord the moon.

sanskrit: sthāṇubhūtaḥ śucir bhūtvā daivatebhyaḥ praṇamya ca gaṅgāyamunayor madhye jalaṃ saṃpraviveśa ha
english: Becoming still as a post, and pure, and bowing to the gods, he entered the water between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyamunayor vegaṃ subhīmaṃ bhīmaniḥsvanam pratijagrāha śirasā vātavegasamaṃ jave
english: The most terrible current of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, with its dreadful roar and a swiftness like the rush of the wind, he received upon his head.

sanskrit: gaṅgā ca yamunā caiva saritaś cānugās tayoḥ pradakṣiṇam ṛṣiṃ cakrur na cainaṃ paryapīḍayan
english: The Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, and the streams that follow after them, made their reverent circuit around the sage and did not afflict him.

sanskrit: antarjale sa suṣvāpa kāṣṭhabhūto mahāmuniḥ tataś cordhvasthito dhīmān abhavad bharatarṣabha
english: Beneath the water the great sage slept, become like a log of wood; and thereafter the wise one stood upright, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: jalaukasāṃ sa sattvānāṃ babhūva priyadarśanaḥ upājighranta ca tadā matsyās taṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ tatra tasyāsataḥ kālaḥ samatīto 'bhavan mahān
english: He became a delight to behold for the creatures that dwell in the water, and the fishes, joyful in heart, came then and nuzzled him; and as he abode there a great span of time passed by.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit samaye kasmiṃś cin matsyajīvinaḥ taṃ deśaṃ samupājagmur jālahastā mahādyute
english: Then, at one time, on a certain occasion, men who lived by fishing came to that region, nets in hand, O greatly radiant one.

sanskrit: niṣādā bahavas tatra matsyoddharaṇaniścitāḥ vyāyatā balinaḥ śūrāḥ salileṣv anivartinaḥ abhyāyayuś ca taṃ deśaṃ niścitā jālakarmaṇi
english: Many Niṣādas, resolved upon hauling up fish, tall, strong, and bold, never turning back in the waters, came to that region, set upon the work of the net.

sanskrit: jālaṃ ca yojayām āsur viśeṣeṇa janādhipa matsyodakaṃ samāsādya tadā bharatasattama
english: And they fastened together their net with special care, O lord of men, having reached the fish-filled water, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas te bahubhir yogaiḥ kaivartā matsyakāṅkṣiṇaḥ gaṅgāyamunayor vāri jālair abhyakiraṃs tataḥ
english: Then those fishermen, craving fish, by many contrivances cast their nets over the waters of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

sanskrit: jālaṃ suvitataṃ teṣāṃ navasūtrakṛtaṃ tathā vistārāyāmasaṃpannaṃ yat tatra salile kṣamam
english: Their net was well-spread, made of new cord, and so fashioned in breadth and length as to be fit for that water.

sanskrit: tatas te sumahac caiva balavac ca suvartitam prakīrya sarvataḥ sarve jālaṃ cakṛṣire tadā
english: Then, having cast it out on every side—that net so very great, so strong, and so well-woven—they all hauled it in together.

sanskrit: abhītarūpāḥ saṃhṛṣṭās te 'nyonyavaśavartinaḥ babandhus tatra matsyāṃś ca tathānyāñ jalacāriṇaḥ
english: Fearless in aspect and full of joy, working in concert one with another, they ensnared therein the fishes and other water-roving creatures as well.

sanskrit: tathā matsyaiḥ parivṛtaṃ cyavanaṃ bhṛgunandanam ākarṣanta mahārāja jālenātha yadṛcchayā
english: And Cyavana, the delight of Bhṛgu's line, surrounded by the fishes, they drew up by chance in their net, O great king.

sanskrit: nadīśaivaladigdhāṅgaṃ hariśmaśrujaṭādharam lagnaiḥ śaṅkhagaṇair gātraiḥ koṣṭhaiś citrair ivāvṛtam
english: His limbs smeared with the river's moss, wearing a tawny beard and matted locks, his body clung about with clusters of shells, as if covered with strange chambered casings.

sanskrit: taṃ jālenoddhṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā te tadā vedapāragam sarve prāñjalayo dāśāḥ śirobhiḥ prāpatan bhuvi
english: Seeing him drawn up in the net, that master of the Vedas, all the fishermen then, with joined palms, fell to the ground with their heads bowed.

sanskrit: parikhedaparitrāsāj jālasyākarṣaṇena ca matsyā babhūvur vyāpannāḥ sthalasaṃkarṣaṇena ca
english: From exhaustion and terror, and from the dragging of the net, and from being hauled onto dry land, the fishes perished.

sanskrit: sa munis tat tadā dṛṣṭvā matsyānāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtam babhūva kṛpayāviṣṭo niḥśvasaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: That sage, beholding the slaughter wrought of the fishes, was overcome with compassion and sighed again and again.

sanskrit: niṣādā ūcuḥ ajñānād yat kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ prasādaṃ tatra naḥ kuru karavāma priyaṃ kiṃ te tan no brūhi mahāmune
english: The Niṣādas said: For the sin that we have done in ignorance, grant us your grace therein. What may we do to please you? Tell us that, O great sage.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity ukto matsyamadhyasthaś cyavano vākyam abravīt yo me 'dya paramaḥ kāmas taṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ samāhitāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, Cyavana, standing amid the fishes, spoke these words: Hear with attentive minds what is now my highest wish.

sanskrit: prāṇotsargaṃ vikrayaṃ vā matsyair yāsyāmy ahaṃ saha saṃvāsān notsahe tyaktuṃ salilādhyuṣitān imān
english: Either to the giving up of life, or to being sold, will I go along with these fishes; for I cannot bear to forsake my companionship with these dwellers in the water.

sanskrit: ity uktās te niṣādās tu subhṛśaṃ bhayakampitāḥ sarve viṣaṇṇavadanā nahuṣāya nyavedayan
english: Thus addressed, those Niṣādas, trembling exceedingly with fear, all of them with downcast faces, made it known to Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nahuṣas tu tataḥ śrutvā cyavanaṃ taṃ tathāgatam tvaritaḥ prayayau tatra sahāmātyapurohitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: And Nahuṣa, hearing then that Cyavana had come to such a pass, set out thither in haste, together with his ministers and his household priest.

sanskrit: śaucaṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyaṃ prāñjaliḥ prayato nṛpaḥ ātmānam ācacakṣe ca cyavanāya mahātmane
english: Having performed his purification as the rule requires, with palms joined and self subdued, the king announced himself to the great-souled Cyavana.

sanskrit: arcayām āsa taṃ cāpi tasya rājñaḥ purohitaḥ satyavrataṃ mahābhāgaṃ devakalpaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: And that king's household priest also honored him—true to his vow, greatly blessed, and godlike, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca karavāṇi priyaṃ kiṃ te tan me vyākhyātum arhasi sarvaṃ kartāsmi bhagavan yady api syāt suduṣkaram
english: Nahuṣa said: What may I do to please you? That you must explain to me. I shall do it all, O blessed one, even though it be most hard to accomplish.

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca śrameṇa mahatā yuktāḥ kaivartā matsyajīvinaḥ mama mūlyaṃ prayacchaibhyo matsyānāṃ vikrayaiḥ saha
english: Cyavana said: The fishermen who live by fish are joined to great toil; pay them my price, together with the price of the fishes.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca sahasraṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyaṃ niṣādebhyaḥ purohita niṣkrayārthaṃ bhagavato yathāha bhṛgunandanaḥ
english: Nahuṣa said: Let a thousand be given as the price to the Niṣādas, O priest, for the ransom of the blessed one, even as the delight of Bhṛgu's line has said.

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca sahasraṃ nāham arhāmi kiṃ vā tvaṃ manyase nṛpa sadṛśaṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyaṃ svabuddhyā niścayaṃ kuru
english: Cyavana said: I am not worth a thousand—or how do you reckon it, O king? Let a fitting price be given; make your determination by your own judgment.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca sahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ kṣipraṃ niṣādebhyaḥ pradīyatām syād etat tu bhaven mūlyaṃ kiṃ vānyan manyate bhavān
english: Nahuṣa said: Let a hundred thousand be given at once to the Niṣādas. Might this then be the price? Or does your honor reckon otherwise?

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca nāhaṃ śatasahasreṇa nimeyaḥ pārthivarṣabha dīyatāṃ sadṛśaṃ mūlyam amātyaiḥ saha cintaya
english: Cyavana said: I am not to be valued at a hundred thousand, O bull among rulers. Let a fitting price be given; consider it together with your ministers.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca koṭiḥ pradīyatāṃ mūlyaṃ niṣādebhyaḥ purohita yad etad api naupamyam ato bhūyaḥ pradīyatām
english: Nahuṣa said: Let a crore be given as the price to the Niṣādas, O priest; and if even this is no fit measure for you, let yet more than this be given.

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca rājan nārhāmy ahaṃ koṭiṃ bhūyo vāpi mahādyute sadṛśaṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha cintaya
english: Cyavana said: O king, I am not worth a crore, nor even more, O greatly radiant one. Let a fitting price be given; consider it together with the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca ardharājyaṃ samagraṃ vā niṣādebhyaḥ pradīyatām etan mūlyam ahaṃ manye kiṃ vānyan manyase dvija
english: Nahuṣa said: Let half the kingdom, or the whole of it, be given to the Niṣādas. This I deem to be the price—or do you reckon otherwise, O twice-born?

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca ardharājyaṃ samagraṃ vā nāham arhāmi pārthiva sadṛśaṃ dīyatāṃ mūlyam ṛṣibhiḥ saha cintyatām
english: Cyavana said: I am not worth half the kingdom, nor the whole, O ruler. Let a fitting price be given; let it be pondered together with the sages.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca maharṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā nahuṣo duḥkhakarśitaḥ sa cintayām āsa tadā sahāmātyapurohitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing the great sage's words, Nahuṣa, worn with distress, then fell to pondering, together with his ministers and his household priest.

sanskrit: tatra tv anyo vanacaraḥ kaś cin mūlaphalāśanaḥ nahuṣasya samīpastho gavijāto 'bhavan muniḥ
english: But there a certain other forest-dweller, who lived on roots and fruits, came to stand near Nahuṣa—a sage born of a cow.

sanskrit: sa samābhāṣya rājānam abravīd dvijasattamaḥ toṣayiṣyāmy ahaṃ vipraṃ yathā tuṣṭo bhaviṣyati
english: That best of the twice-born, addressing the king, said: I shall satisfy the Brāhmaṇa, so that he shall be content.
